q-69453.name: Question 1
q-69453.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/70fe7561f7019a01ea671190c26e3d73f8918fcd18172d0c3e3a1a9447d7269e.png)

The diagram above shows the vectors $a$ and $b.$ Which of the following diagrams illustrates the vector addition $a+b.$
q-69453.worked_solution:
First, we draw the vector that is equal to $b$ and has its tail placed at the head of $a.$ 

Now, according to the triangle law of addition, the resultant 

$$
a+b
$$

is the vector that goes from the tail of $\text{a}$ to the head of $\text{b}$, as shown below.

q-118283.name: Question 3
q-118283.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/392fab62a445326d26f7c637735cb03f13d94139ec0141d1802c8617020b1489.png)

Consider the vector $a,$ shown above. Which of the following could be $a+(-a)?$
q-118283.worked_solution:
According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant is the vector that goes from the tail of $a$ to the head of $-a.$ 

Therefore, we obtain a new vector for which the tail and head is the same point, the tail of $a.$ 

That vector is called the zero vector, and we write

$$
a+(-a)=0.
$$

The corresponding graph is shown below.

q-118289.name: Question 5
q-118289.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/bb7d3c1f1cf1ed19c22bad9eefc9f8c4911d70ed74231c5d63ed88a6cd710a67.png)

The diagram shows the vectors $a$ and $b.$  Which of the following diagrams illustrates the vector subtraction $-a+b.$
q-118289.worked_solution:
We interpret  $-a+b$ as the addition

$$
(-a)+b,
$$

where $-a$ is the vector that has the same magnitude as $a$ but goes in the direction *opposite* of $a.$

Finally, we use the triangle law to add the vectors $-a$ and $b:$ 

- We can start $-a$ from an arbitrary point on the plane.

- Next, we draw the vector that is equal to $b$ and has its tail placed at the head of $-a.$

- Now, according to the triangle law of addition, the resultant is the vector that goes from the tail of $-\text{a}$ to the head of $\text{b}$, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/9a5dc1c9f479702ef746df13ca445b3fea68e0452e36e51ddff2622a19f24a84.png)

  • Next, we draw the vector that is equal to b and has its tail placed at the head of −a.

We interpret the subtraction

$$

where $-b$ is the vector that has the same magnitude as $b$ but goes in the direction *opposite* of $b.$

Finally, we use the triangle law to add the vectors $a$ and $-b:$ 

- We can start $a$ from an arbitrary point on the plane.

q-69482.name: Question 7
q-69482.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/6f1af14d60c9b2353d3aa149c4f74ead097289fd2a619013f1506cb783b72ee2.png)

The vectors $\text{a},$ $\text{b},$ and $\text{c}$ are shown in the diagram above. Which of the following diagrams shows the vector $a-b-c.$
q-69482.worked_solution:
First, we use the triangle law of addition to find 

$$
a-b=a+(-b).
$$

The resultant $a-b$ is the vector that joins the tail of $\text{a}$ and the head of $-\text{b}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/0f1c13ae5c58b1745ac8582d1ba7fd1fc4d8c1fe434adea2aa125d5025a0859a.png)

Now, we use the triangle law of addition to find 

$$
(\text{a}-\text{b})-\text{c}=(\text{a}-\text{b})+(-\text{c}).
$$

We draw $-\text{c}$ from the head of $\text{a}-\text{b}.$ So, we have the vector that goes from the tail of $\text{a}$ to the head of $-\text{c}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196443/assets/da52e611ffe7002e478024073ec134e4f5b6a6d1b12f19513fed24a0b03ba25b.png)
